subject.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths

question: Should isolated cron treat clean empty assistant replies as silent success for all cron jobs, including deliver/announce jobs, or only for explicitly silent/no-deliver jobs?
rationale: The code shape is narrow and well-covered, but the behavior change is an intentional product policy choice with compatibility and message-delivery implications.

options.title: Adopt all-cron silent success
options.body: Land this PR as the canonical fix if empty cron output means nothing to report for both no-deliver and deliver jobs.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Change the flag to follow `delivery.mode === "none"`, no-deliver, or another explicit silent signal if visible-delivery cron jobs should still fail on empty output.

options.title: Pause for a per-job option
options.body: Hold this PR if operators need an explicit per-job opt-in or opt-out surface with docs and migration guidance.

recommendation.title: Adopt all-cron silent success
recommendation.body: Land this PR as the canonical fix if empty cron output means nothing to report for both no-deliver and deliver jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this owner to both the cron executor and silent-reply runtime surfaces that define the policy boundary.
